title: S3 from C#
description: Upload, download, list, and delete S3 objects using the AWSSDK.S3 NuGet package.

data.text: Amazon S3 is ideal for user uploads, report files, and static assets. The `AWSSDK.S3` package provides high-level and granular clients for every S3 operation.

data.title: Upload and download an object
data.content: Use `AmazonS3Client` for common S3 operations. This example includes a service class with constructor injection, try/catch error handling, and cancellation token support.

data.title: List and delete objects in a bucket
data.content: Paginate through objects and remove old files. This example includes a dedicated service class with error handling.

data.text: A presigned URL gives a client temporary access to a single object without exposing your AWS credentials.

data.title: Generate a presigned download URL
data.content: Use `GetPreSignedURL` to create a time-limited download link. Includes error handling and expected output comments.

data.title: Build a file upload endpoint
data.description: Create an API endpoint that accepts an IFormFile and stores it in S3.
steps: Create a new controller action accepting `IFormFile`
Instantiate `AmazonS3Client` inside the action or through DI
Upload the file to the S3 bucket
Return the S3 key or presigned URL to the caller
data.expectedOutcome: The uploaded file appears in the S3 bucket and can be downloaded by URL.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Always use async APIs for upload and download
Use presigned URLs when clients need temporary direct access
Store bucket names and keys as constants or configuration
data.takeaway: S3 turns your ASP.NET Core app into a file management system without any server-side disk management.
